lines.text: Use of Language
Conjunctions:
Remember!
We use words called conjunctions,
like'and, 'or,'"but,"because'and
'although,; to join two parts of
sentences.
Conjunctions can be used to give
moreinformation,give
alternatives, give reasons,give
resultsorgiveunexpected
information.
in order to: to express purpose or intention.
Example: He saved money in order to buy a new car.
where: indicate a place or location.
Example: We visited a park where we could have a picnic.
wherever: to indicate any place or location.
Example: She can work from home wherever she is.
if: to introduce a conditional clause.
Example: If it rains, we will stay indoors.
until: to indicate the duration of an action or condition.
Example: She waited until the movie started before entering the theater.
unless: used to express a condition that must be met.
Example: You won't pass the test unless you study.
therefore: used to indicate a cause-and-effect relationship or conclusion
Example: He studied hard; therefore, he performed well in the exam.
since: used to indicate a cause-and-effect relationship or time.
Example: Since it was his birthday, we threw him a surprise party.
